steps.say: A GoPro, carried through a shopping mall. No LiDAR, no calibration target.
The map on the right is built from its video and its own IMU, as the camera walks.
steps.caption: GoPro walk, Accord's map beside it

scenes.headline: Where a camera-and-IMU map gets its metres
scenes.sub: Accord: a filter for the poses, a depth model for the surfaces
scenes.say: I'm Baseline. Accord makes dense metric maps from one camera and an IMU, and every metre in them comes from one place.

left.title: Visual-inertial odometry
left.say: A visual-inertial filter knows how far the camera moved, in metres, but its map is a few hundred points.

right.title: Depth foundation model
items: Scale off by a few percent
right.say: A depth model gives every pixel a depth, but even when it is told the poses, its scale is off by a few percent.

stations.label: Window
stations.sub: five keyframes, half a second apart

steps.say: The filter tracks every frame on the CPU, and the map never writes back to it.
Every half second a frame becomes a keyframe, and five of them make a window.
The depth model predicts the window's depth, conditioned on the filter's poses.
Keypoints triangulated under those same poses pull the window onto the filter's scale.
Each window becomes a submap in a graph that loop closures correct.

scenes.title: One wall, six images, three windows

labels: After the depth model and the window fit

steps.say: Six images draw the same wall. After the window fit, each window's copy sits at its own depth.
The anchor gives every window the filter's scale. A few percent per image is left, and at three metres that is several centimetres.
So images from different windows that see one wall are compared, both ways. One correction per image, and the copies fall onto one line.
steps.term: Agreement: half the difference of the two directions

steps.say: What no step can see is the filter's own scale error. The whole map moves with it.
Here is that on a real floor plan. Before the correction, one wall is smeared into layers.
After it, the layers agree, and the map's median distance to the laser scan drops from two point four to one point three centimetres.
On a drone in a Vicon room, the map builds around the flight while the filter keeps tracking.

scenes.title: Map F-score at 5 cm, EuRoC rooms
scenes.note: every map placed by its own trajectory
scenes.say: Scored with each map placed by its own trajectory, Accord has the best mean map on all four scanned datasets, and the runner-up changes every time.

items.say: The scale is the filter's. A better filter would buy a better map.
Depth past twenty metres is dropped, so the far side of a big courtyard stays empty.
And on uncalibrated phones every pipeline scores far lower, Accord included.

scenes.text: The metres come from the filter; the map's job is to make every image agree on them.
scenes.say: The metres come from the filter. The map's job is to make every image agree on them.

recap: Anchor each window to the filter's keypoints
Make overlapping images agree, both ways
Corrections sum to zero, so scale never drifts
scenes.say: Anchor to the filter, make the images agree, and the scale stays put.
